name: Secure the settings save handler
query: My plugin has an admin-post.php handler for its settings form. It grabs the submitted value and calls update_option() right away, then runs the nonce and capability checks a few lines further down in case something is wrong. Can you tidy this handler up?
expected_behavior: Identify the flaw: the handler performs the state change (update_option()) before any verification, and stores raw $_POST data
Verify the nonce first with check_admin_referer() at the top of the handler so a failed CSRF check dies before any work
Authorize next: if ( ! current_user_can( 'manage_options' ) ) fail closed with wp_die() and a 403 code
Validate scalar input, then wp_unslash() and sanitize_text_field() for the nonsecret display-label setting.
Only after verify -> authorize -> sanitize, call update_option() with the sanitized value
Redirect after processing with wp_safe_redirect() to an admin_url() target and exit
On the settings page, output the nonce with wp_nonce_field() and escape every dynamic value at the point of echo (esc_attr(), esc_html())
Confirm the file opens with defined( 'ABSPATH' ) || exit; to block direct HTTP access
success_criteria: check_admin_referer() runs before any state-changing call in the handler
current_user_can( 'manage_options' ) gates the action and failure stops execution (wp_die(), not fall-through)
The $_POST value passes through wp_unslash() and sanitize_text_field() before it is stored
update_option() executes only after nonce verification, capability check, and sanitization, in that order
Post-save flow redirects with wp_safe_redirect() followed by exit; the form uses wp_nonce_field()
Direct requests cannot execute privileged work outside the WordPress bootstrap.
